info.name: EventManager — System Test (all units)
info.description:
End-to-end HTTP coverage for the EventManager MVP plus post-MVP unit U9 (Read/Query API), mirroring aidlc-docs/testing-guide.md.

Two hosts:
- **Cloud backend** (U3 + U8) at {{cloudBaseUrl}} — behind the TLS proxy from `docker compose up` (see backend/.env). Bearer-auth; register/confirm/login/refresh are anonymous.
- **Admin hub** (U4a + U4b) at {{hubBaseUrl}} — `dotnet run --project admin/EventManager.Hub`. No auth on the LAN surface.

Run order matters: Login captures the token; Create Event / Configure Division / Athlete Profile / Register capture ids into collection variables that later requests reuse. Test scripts do the capturing automatically.

Units with no HTTP surface (U7 resilience, U5/U6 spoke app-cores) are verified via `dotnet test` — see §4/§5 of the testing guide; there is nothing to call here for them.

item.name: Read API (U9)
item.description:
Unit U9 — nine GET endpoints over the read models, governed by a three-tier access model.

**Tiers** (cumulative, resolved per event):
- **Public** — any authenticated caller, event registration Open. Event *summary*, divisions, weigh-in policy.
- **Registrant** — caller holds a non-withdrawn registration. Adds event *detail* and their own registration.
- **Organizer** — caller holds an organizer role. Adds the full roster and the organizer roster.

**Two conventions differ from the write endpoints:**
1. Insufficient tier returns **404, never 403** — a 403 would confirm the resource exists (US-709).
2. Response *shape* follows from the resolved tier, not from anything you send.

Run 5-13 in the Cloud Backend folder first so `eventId`, `divisionId`, and `registrationId` are populated. To exercise the tier model properly, log in as a second account that is neither an organizer nor a registrant of {{eventId}} and re-run — the roster and account requests must return 404.

request.description: US-704. Union of Public + Registrant + Organizer events, each tagged with `accessTier` and, where held, `organizerRole`. Complete and unpaginated (Q7=A). No ETag — the result spans multiple event scopes with no single watermark.

exec: pm.test('every item carries an access tier', () => pm.expect(items.every(i => !!i.accessTier)).to.be.true);
pm.test('no ETag on the cross-scope collection', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('ETag')).to.be.false);

request.description:
US-701/702/703. Public callers get the **summary** shape; Registrant and Organizer get **detail** (adds cardEnabled, checkInStarted, weighInPolicy, createdByAccountId).

Captures the ETag into `eventEtag` for request 18.

exec: console.log(b.cardEnabled === undefined ? 'tier: Public (summary shape)' : 'tier: Registrant/Organizer (detail shape)');

request.description:
US-710. Replays the ETag captured by request 17. A match returns **304 with no body**, and no read-model table is queried to produce it.

Set the `If-None-Match` header to `{{eventEtag}}` (already configured below).

The ETag covers `(endpoint, eventId, watermark, tier, flags)` — not the watermark alone. If you register for this event and re-run request 17, the ETag **changes**, because your tier changed. That is deliberate: a watermark-only tag would return 304 here and silently withhold the detail fields you just earned.
US-705. Public tier and above. Completed divisions are excluded by default; add `?includeCompleted=true` to include them (BR-READ-15).
US-705 with the inclusion flag. Returns divisions whose status is Complete as well.
US-705. The id must belong to {{eventId}} — a division that exists under a different event returns 404 here, so cross-event probing reveals nothing (BR-READ-19).

US-706. Public tier and above — a prospective registrant needs the policy to judge the risk of competing at their current weight.

`tolerancePercent` is present **only** when `mode` is Tolerance. There is no collection form of this resource: an event has exactly one policy.

exec: else pm.expect(p.tolerancePercent == null).to.be.true;   // null or omitted

request.description:
US-707. **Organizer tier only** — Public and Registrant callers get 404, not 403.

The list shape carries no date of birth, weight, rank, or gender; those appear only on the detail endpoint (request 23). Withdrawn registrations are excluded unless `?includeWithdrawn=true`.

Note: registrations whose managing account has been **deleted** are still returned. Account deletion anonymizes the identity record only — the athlete is still competing and must appear on the roster.

exec: pm.test('200 OK for an organizer', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('list shape omits profile fields', () => pm.expect(rows.every(r => r.weight === undefined && r.dateOfBirth === undefined)).to.be.true);

request.description: US-707 with the inclusion flag. Withdrawn registrations are returned and identifiable via the `withdrawn` field.

US-707. Adds dateOfBirth, weight, rank, gender. Readable by an Organizer for any registration, or by a Registrant **only for their own** records.

**This endpoint deliberately issues no ETag** (U9-CON-2). Athlete profile events are appended with the *athlete* id as their scope, not the event id, so the event watermark does not move when an athlete edits their weight — a conditional response could return 304 carrying a stale weight. Rather than paper over that, the endpoint is excluded from conditional handling.

US-708. Organizer tier only. One entry per account holding an organizer role, with accountId, email, and role.

Scoped strictly to this event's roster. The original request was 'any account by id'; that was rejected at requirements as a blocking SECURITY-08 finding, because it would let any organizer probe arbitrary account ids and learn which accounts exist.

exec: pm.test('200 OK for an organizer', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('no credential material is ever returned', () => pm.expect(rows.every(r =>
r.passwordHash === undefined && r.securityStamp === undefined && r.twoFactorEnabled === undefined)).to.be.true);

request.description: US-708. Returns 404 for an account that exists but holds **no organizer role on this event** — this endpoint never confirms the existence of unrelated accounts (BR-READ-10). Set `coOrganizerAccountId` from the 'Add co-organizer' request first.

exec: pm.test('200 for a real co-organizer, 404 otherwise', () => pm.expect([200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description:
US-709. An event id that does not exist and an event you hold no tier on return the **same 404 with the same body** — the two cases are indistinguishable, so probing reveals nothing.

To see the other half: close registration on an event you do not administer, then request it. The response must be byte-identical to this one.
US-709 / BR-READ-19. Set `otherDivisionId` to a division belonging to a **different** event, then run this. A valid id under the wrong event path returns 404 — never 403, and never the resource.

US-709. Re-run this while authenticated as a Public or Registrant caller — someone who is **not** an organizer of {{eventId}}. The roster must return 404, not 403.

Swap `accessToken` for a second account's token first; otherwise this is request 22 and will return 200.

exec: pm.test('404 for a non-organizer, 200 for an organizer', () => pm.expect([200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Hub Replication (U10)

request.description: US-801. Issues an event-scoped hub credential. The key is returned EXACTLY ONCE and only a hash is stored, so it cannot be retrieved again - the test captures it into {{hubCredentialKey}}.
US-801 / BR-REPL-24. Listing shows label, dates and derived state - never key material.

exec: pm.test('no key material in any row', () => pm.expect(rows.every(r => !('key' in r) && !('keyHash' in r))).to.be.true);
pm.test('state is derived, not stored', () => pm.expect(rows.every(r => ['Active','Expired','Revoked'].includes(r.state))).to.be.true);

item.name: 33. Ingest a batch as the hub

request.description: US-803 / U10-FR-1. A batch authenticated by the HUB credential rather than an organizer JWT.
US-803 / BR-REPL-44. Re-sending is always safe: the cloud gains nothing and reports the same progress.
US-805 / U10-FR-12. Lets a restarted hub resume from where the cloud actually is instead of re-sending the whole event. A hub credential is already bound to one event, so it does not name it.

item.name: 36. NEGATIVE - batch for a different event is refused ENTIRELY

request.description: US-809 / BR-REPL-10. A batch containing ANY foreign scope is refused whole - no partial acceptance, because a batch is the unit of atomic intent.
US-809 / BR-REPL-7. Unknown, expired and revoked all produce the SAME generic failure, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which credentials exist.
US-808. Revocation is immediate and one-way - there is no un-revoke, the remedy is to issue a new credential. Already-replicated data is unaffected and the hub keeps running the event locally.

item.name: 39. NEGATIVE - revoked credential refused on the very next request

request.description: US-808 / BR-REPL-8. Authentication is evaluated per request with no session or cache, which is what makes revocation effective immediately.
US-802. Closes U10-CON-5. Installing over an existing credential is REFUSED (409) - clear it first.
US-806. Computed on demand, and computable with NO internet - the one question asked during an outage must be answerable during an outage. Never echoes the credential.
US-807. Drives replication to completion within a bounded window, then reports whether the cloud holds 100%. Always returns - at a venue, an honest incomplete beats a call that never comes back.

exec: pm.test('200 OK or no credential installed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 409]));

request.description: US-802 / FD-Q8=B. The other half of refuse-rather-than-overwrite: clearing is an explicit, separate action, so a working credential cannot be destroyed by a careless paste.

item.description: Unit U10 - hub identity and cloud replication. Issuing an event-scoped hub credential, installing it on the hub, ingesting as a hub rather than as a person, cursor reads, close-out, revocation, and the negative cases. Run 31 first: it captures the one-time key.
